pixels.cursor_source_verification: Root's explanation is confirmed from source, not by relaxing geometry. The 008 compositor d42795c8 (built from the unchanged sources/chonkstep-darwin) enables the pointer seat in enable_pdhid_seat (input.rs:44-52): seat.add_pointer() and backend cursor = Some((Point::new(0,0), arrow())). The scene starts the pointer at Point::new(0,0) (scene.rs:64) and, after all windows and decorations, draws the cursor at pointer - hotspot = (0,0) (scene.rs:225-226), so it sits over the title bar's left control. arrow() (input.rs:21-25) is a 12x18 RGBA buffer: rows 0-15, columns 0..min(y*2/3,10), shade 0 on edges and 255 inside, alpha 0 elsewhere. The keyboard-only compositor 717da106 (isolated source = approved patch 15fe9556) replaces this with enable_pdhid_seat_caps (input.rs:50-61): pointer only 'if caps.pointer', and 'if caps.pointer{b.cursor=Some((Point::new(0,0),arrow()));}'. With --input pdhid-keyboard, caps.pointer is false, so cursor stays at its initial None (scene.rs:64) and the draw at scene.rs:225 never runs. A client cannot set a cursor either, because set_cursor needs a wl_pointer and the seat advertises none. Pixel proof: composing exactly that arrow() at (0,0) over this capture reproduces 008's top-left 16x24 area with 0 mismatches. That accounts for 53 changed pixels at x 1-8, y 2-18 (008 white 255/black edges vs this capture's button 80/black), the same 53 root counted. The right button cells and everything else outside the title text are identical to 008.
